hard_validation_attempt_1.text: The guard captain shrugs slightly, a faint smile breaking through the weathered lines on their face. "There's just something about the rain beating down on the old stones, the feel of those frayed banners overhead," they say. "It reminds me that this place has stood through worse—storms, sieges, and all. Watching the gate in this rain, despite the cold and wet, feels like standing guard not just for today, but for all the days before and those still to come. It holds a certain stubborn pride that the walls inside, cozy as they are, just can't match."

hard_validation_attempt_2.text: Rain spatters soot-dark stone; frayed banners hang above Cinderwatch's eastern gate. Refugees, wagons, and foot traffic clog the muddy approach; guards hold the choke while the crowd presses in. A notice board lists new taxes, curfews, and a posted warning about a missing patrol. Nearby, a tavern runner shouts offers of hot stew and paid rumor. Across the square, a well-appointed townhouse flies noble colors, standing out quietly against the muddy clamor. One figure in threadbare clothes remains unusually still, their gaze flicking toward packs and faces more than the gate queue.
